citation: Wijekumar, K., Hitchcock, J., Turner, H., Lei, P. W., & Peck, K. (2009). A multisite cluster randomized trial of the effects of CompassLearning Odyssey® Math on the math achievement of selected grade 4 students in the Mid-Atlantic region. Final report (NCEE 2009-4068). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. Prepared by Regional Educational Laboratory Mid-Atlantic, Pennsylvania State University (contract ED-06C0-0029).
report_number: NCEE 2009-4068 (REL Mid-Atlantic); ERIC ED507314; reviewed in WWC Intervention Report 'Odyssey Math' (Aug 2009), WWC study record 71018.
design: Multisite cluster (school-block) randomized controlled trial. Within each of 32 participating elementary/intermediate/charter schools in the Mid-Atlantic region (PA 23, NJ 8, DE 1), all grade-4 teachers' classrooms were randomly assigned WITHIN school to intervention (CompassLearning Odyssey Math, a web-based computer math curriculum/digital tool used ~60 min/week as a partial substitute for the regular math curriculum) or control (same regular math curriculum, no Odyssey). Random assignment at the teacher/classroom level blocked by school = 'School' assignment unit in the meta-analysis registry. TPD-FOR-DIGITAL-TOOLS component: intervention teachers received five 'days' of CompassLearning professional development to deliver Odyssey Math -- a summer large-group session (~5-6 hrs/day) plus in-class individual coaching sessions during the school year (Aug 2007 - Mar 2008; see Table 9 / Appendix A). Control teachers received the SAME professional development only AFTER the study (delayed-treatment / business-as-usual counterfactual). Subject = mathematics (-> STEM); grade 4 (registry grade band coded 3-6). Outcome = TerraNova CTBS Basic Battery math subtest (CTB/McGraw-Hill 2000), Form A, scaled scores level 14, administered Sep-Oct 2007 (pretest) and Apr-May 2008 (posttest); standardized norm-referenced test (KR20=.93, sample alpha=.91), independent of the developer. Analytic sample: 32 schools, 122 teachers (60 intervention / 62 control), 2,456 students (1,223 intervention / 1,233 control) with both pre- and posttest. Impact estimated via 3-level HLM (students in classrooms in schools) with class-mean pretest covariate, random intervention effect across schools -> clustering accounted for. WWC: meets standards without reservations.
problems: STUDY-IDENTITY CORRECTION (important): The assignment brief assumed 'Wijekumar et al. 2009' = the ITSS / Intelligent Tutoring for the Structure Strategy reading-comprehension software and instructed to extract Reading outcomes only. That assumption is INCORRECT for this row. The only 2009 Wijekumar-first-author publication is the NCEE/REL Mid-Atlantic final report on CompassLearning ODYSSEY MATH (NCEE 2009-4068, ERIC ED507314) -- a grade-4 MATH digital-tool RCT, not an ITSS reading study. The ITSS reading RCTs by this team are the PUBLISHED journal articles (Wijekumar, Meyer & Lei 2012 ETR&D grade-4; 2013 Computers&Education grade-4/5; 2014 JREE grade-5; 2017 grade-7) -- those are coded as separate registry rows (e.g. row 135 = Wijekumar et al. 2017). This row 134 is decisively identified as the Odyssey Math report by the registry descriptors, which match it exactly and NOT any ITSS study: Unpublished (NCEE technical report, not a journal article), School-level assignment (cluster RCT blocked within 32 schools), grade band 3-6 (grade 4 falls in 3-6), 'TPD for digital tools' (Odyssey is a web-based digital tool and intervention teachers got CompassLearning PD to use it; ITSS journal studies are coded 'TPD for curricula'), 'Short' duration, and 'One' (single confirmatory contrast / single timepoint). Therefore the qualifying student-achievement outcome here is MATH (outcome_subject='STEM'), not Reading. There are no reading/literacy outcomes in this report. The two exploratory questions (gender; low- vs medium/high-scoring subgroups) are NOT analyzed in this report -- the report states (p.6) they 'will be addressed in a separate report' -- so there are no subgroup effect sizes to extract here; only the single full-sample confirmatory math contrast exists. RESULT: TPD-for-digital-tools (Odyssey Math) had NO statistically significant effect on grade-4 math achievement (Hedges' g ≈ 0.02, p=.54). MINOR NUMERIC NUANCE: The report gives two near-identical pretest-adjusted impact coefficients for the same confirmatory model: Table 12 bottom row / chapter-4 narrative report γ010=0.78 (SE=1.27, p=.543) -- this is the report's HEADLINE adjusted impact and is what I used; the 'complete' parameter table J1 (Appendix J) reports γ010=0.80 (SE=1.47, t31=0.55, p=.588) for the full random-coefficients model. Both standardize to effect size 0.02 by the authors. I used the headline 0.78/1.27 for g and g_se. CLUSTER/ICC: impact SE is from the multilevel model so cluster_adjusted=true; teacher-level ICC=0.12 and school-level ICC=0.05 are reported (Appendix I, Table I1) and recorded. n_clusters: assignment is at the teacher/classroom level (122 classrooms) blocked within 32 schools; I record n_clusters=32 (schools, the top design level) and note 122 teachers/classrooms in notes.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CompassLearning Odyssey Math (web-based digital math tool) + 5 days CompassLearning teacher PD vs business-as-usual regular math curriculum (control teachers received the same PD only after the study)
effect_sizes.test_name: TerraNova CTBS Basic Battery, math subtest, Form A (CTB/McGraw-Hill 2000); scaled scores, level 14 (grade 4); norm-referenced standardized test
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring, Apr-May 2008; end of the single 2007-08 school-year intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Pretest-adjusted (ANCOVA-style 3-level HLM) impact estimate divided by the student-level pooled within-group posttest SD, exactly as the authors define it (p.~22, line: 'effect size was computed as a standardized mean difference (Hedge's g) by dividing the adjusted group mean difference (gamma010) by the pooled within-intervention and control group standard deviation of the student-level outcome score'). Numerator gamma010 = 0.78 TerraNova scale points (Table 12 bottom row / chapter 4; SE=1.27); standardizing SD = pooled student-level posttest SD = 38.69 (p.41). d = 0.78/38.69 = 0.02016. Hedges' J = 1 - 3/(4*df - 1) with df ~ 2454 (N=2456-2) ~ 0.99969, so g = J*d = 0.02015 ~ 0.02, matching the authors' reported effect size of 0.02. g_se = impact_se / standardizing_SD = 1.27/38.69 = 0.03283; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.001078. This SE is taken from the multilevel-model impact SE, which accounts for student-within-classroom-within-school clustering (cluster_adjusted=true). Adjusted posttest means (Table 12): intervention 648.29, control 647.50 (diff 0.78 after class-mean pretest adjustment); unadjusted posttest means 647.41 vs 646.60 (diff 0.81, SE 2.36). The authors did not report a separate intervention-group posttest SD (control student-level SD=38.18; pooled=38.69), so sd_t is left null.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 12, p.40-41 (adjusted posttest impact gamma010=0.78, SE=1.27, p=.543, ES 0.02); pooled posttest SD 38.69 / control SD 38.18 on p.41; analytic sample (1,223 int / 1,233 ctrl, 122 teachers, 32 schools) Table 7 p.16 & p.40; Hedges' g definition p.~22; ICC 0.12 (teacher) / 0.05 (school) Appendix I Table I1 p.71; complete-model gamma010=0.80 SE=1.47 in Appendix J Table J1 p.72.
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY and ONLY student-achievement contrast in this report: the single confirmatory question (Do grade-4 Odyssey Math classrooms outperform control classrooms on the TerraNova math subtest?). Intent-to-treat, full sample. Result is essentially null: adjusted impact 0.78 scale points (<1 point), Hedges' g ~0.02, NOT statistically significant (p=.54); the study had 80%+ power to detect MDE=0.20 and found no effect. This is a MATH (STEM) outcome -- there are NO reading outcomes in this report (see 'problems': the assignment brief's ITSS/reading assumption does not apply to this row; row 134 = the CompassLearning Odyssey Math NCEE report). The two exploratory subgroup questions (gender; low vs medium/high scorers) were deferred to a separate report and are not analyzed here, so no subgroup effect sizes exist. Random assignment was at the teacher/classroom level (122 classrooms) blocked within 32 schools (registry codes assignment unit = 'School'); n_clusters recorded as 32 schools (top design level). icc=0.12 is the teacher/classroom-level ICC; school-level ICC=0.05. g_var/g_se derived from the multilevel-model impact SE (already clustering-adjusted).
